churn_resistance.rationale: Data access is behind one well-defined, typed module and config is centralized, so framework or requirement changes touch few files. It loses a point on internals and silence: one read of an undocumented router internal, untyped API payloads inside the server module, and validators that assert rather than validate mean upstream changes fail loudly instead of at compile time.

findings.issue: Reads m._notFound, an underscore-prefixed internal field, to set the not-found title; undocumented internals like this are the ones the framework removes without a deprecation notice (cf. 1.171.16's removal of RouterState.statusCode).
findings.suggestion: Drop the m._notFound check and rely on the public match.status === 'notFound' (documented RouteMatch status union), or move the fallback title into the notFoundComponent via a child head.

findings.issue: PokeAPI responses are typed `any` end to end (get, latestFlavorText, englishEffect, chainNode, all the list parsers), so a schema or field rename upstream is invisible to the compiler and surfaces only as runtime undefineds in pages.
findings.suggestion: Declare minimal interfaces for the PokeAPI records actually consumed (species, pokemon, move, type, generation) so changes fail where the data enters, keeping the hand-rolled flexibility.

findings.issue: The validator is an identity cast (data: ListFilters) => data; the name-based ones coerce with String() but no field is actually checked, so malformed query values cross the network boundary unchecked.
findings.suggestion: Validate explicitly (zod, or per-field checks like app/src/routes/index.tsx:11 already does for search params) — the docs recommend schema validation precisely because these are network endpoints.

findings.issue: Static serving is gated on the literal /assets/ prefix, silently coupled to Vite's default assetsDir; a build config change or the plugin moving hashed files elsewhere would 404 CSS/JS through the SSR handler.
findings.suggestion: Serve the whole dist/client tree as fall-through middleware (srvx staticMiddleware returns undefined on miss) or read the assets dir from the Vite config rather than assuming the prefix.

findings.issue: No errorComponent is defined anywhere; if the PokeAPI server errors or is down, users get the framework's default error page instead of a branded one.
findings.suggestion: Add a root errorComponent (as the official start-basic example does) so upstream API failures degrade gracefully.

findings.issue: Query strings are hand-split and re-glued for the cache key instead of using URLSearchParams.
findings.suggestion: Build/cache on URL or URLSearchParams objects; removes the string surgery and normalizes edge cases.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache only prunes when size exceeds 5000 entries and only removes already-expired items, so memory grows unbounded toward that cap between prunes.
findings.suggestion: Prune expired entries on insert (or use an LRU bound) — one line, removes the growth ceiling.

summary: This is current-generation TanStack Start code: post-RC server functions with .validator(), head()-based meta, file routes with loaderDeps-driven search state, and the lean React 19/Vite 8/srvx stack, with no legacy APIs left behind. Data access is cleanly isolated behind one typed server module, so most future changes stay local. What keeps it from exemplary is a single internal router field read, untyped upstream API payloads, pass-through validators at the network boundary, and a small amount of build-output coupling in the hand-rolled production server.
